articles.title: Novak Djokovic: Seven-time Rolex Paris Masters champion keeps chances of making ATP Finals in Turin alive
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic keeps alive his hopes of qualifying for the ATP Finals with a comeback victory over Valentin Vacherot in the first round of the Paris Masters as Arthur Fery suffers an early exit; You can watch the ATP Paris Masters live on Sky Sports this week
articles.body:
The seven-time Paris champion was pushed hard by the Monegasque and overcame a mid-match shoulder issue to defeat the Basel champion 6-7 (5-7) 7-5 6-1.

Djokovic requires at least a semi-final run in Paris to give himself a chance of qualifying for the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin.

Djokovic is 11th in the Race To Turin on 2,940 points but must finish inside the top nine to qualify. Rafael Jodar, still alive in Paris, is currently ninth on 3,234 points, 294 points clear of Djokovic.

Asked on Sky Sports how he was feeling physically, Djokovic, who next plays Australian Rinky Hijikata , said: "Not the freshest but obviously glad to turn this match around.

"A lot of players tell me it's completely different conditions to what it was last year.

"It's very slow and bouncy this year, just super, super quick, and Vacherot won his tournament title in Basel a few days ago, super confident and you could feel that in his game, particularly off that first serve. Not too many double faults, he's going for his second serve as well.

"His third serve is quicker than my first so it's very difficult to face someone like that. I should have taken that first set, just an awful volley at 5-4 and next thing you know you're down a set and down a break."

"I'm glad that I kind of found a way to turn this match around."

"Djokovic is so used to being seeded high and at least get himself into the draw without having to suffer through that first round. This is a physical match, and if he wants to go deep in the tournament, especially here in Paris because this is a shorter Masters tournament 1000. This isn't one of those Masters tournaments where you have a day off between every match, so this is going to be a little tricker for him."

British No 1 Arthur Fery may have hit a career-high world No 32 and produced the shot of the match with a between-the-legs drop-shot winner, but he was ultimately taken out by home favourite Quentin Halys 7-6 (8-6) 7-5.

Fery was unable to take two set points in the first-set tie-break with big-serving Frenchman Halys claiming the only break of serve in the second for victory.

British No 2 Cameron Norrie also made an early exit, as he was swept aside 6-3 6-4 by US Open finalist Ben Shelton .

Shelton, who has captured four tour-level titles, including his second ATP Masters 1000 crown in Canada and reached a maiden Grand Slam final at the US Open this year, announced that he will add Alcaraz's former mentor Juan Carlos Ferrero to his team in 2027.

"Juan Carlos is one of the great minds in tennis," Shelton said.

"His experience of winning at the highest level and developing champions will be a huge asset to our team."

Ferrero said: "Ben has extraordinary talent, power and character. I'm looking forward to contributing my experience and working together with everyone to help Ben achieve his ambitions."

Taylor Fritz rallied from a set down to defeat French qualifier Benjamin Bonzi 3-6 6-3 6-4 to reach the second round where he faces another qualifier, Alex Molcan .

Tommy Paul , currently 13th in the Race To Turin on 2,775 points, beat Holger Rune 7-5 6-4.

Flavio Cobolli has announced his withdrawal from the Masters 1000 event on social media.

"I was really hoping I could make it," Cobolli wrote in his Instagram Stories. "Today, after media day, I tried training in the gym, but I'm still feeling some discomfort and I don't want to take any risks. So I've decided to withdraw from Paris.

"This one really hurts. This city gave me the two biggest weeks of my career this year, and playing here again would have meant a lot. Now it's all about recovering. Thank you for always being there."

Despite his withdrawal from the ATP Masters 1000 event in Paris, Cobolli remains in contention to make his Nitto ATP Finals debut.

The Italian is currently sixth in the Race To Turin, 466 points ahead of ninth-placed Rafael Jodar, who is effectively in the final qualification spot.

Britain's Jodie Burrage suffered a first-round loss in a gruelling encounter at the Chennai Open on Tuesday.

Taking on local wild card Vaishnavi Adkar , Britain's Burrage looked poised for victory when she led 5-3 in the deciding set but she lost four games in a row to fall to a 3-6 6-3 7-5 defeat after two hours and 47 minutes.

Burrage, who has not won a tour-level match since Eastbourne last summer, appeared to struggle with the humid conditions and called the doctor with her opponent about to serve for the match.

Burrage was visibly shaking and had her blood pressure and oxygen levels checked as well as ice rubbed on her arms and legs. She was able to resume the contest but lost the final game to love.

articles.title: WTA Chennai Open: US junior star fights on to make a mark
articles.summary: By Jedidah Joshem CHENNAI: Once touted as the future of American tennis, Robin Montgomery is now on a mission to make her mark on the senior circuit.
articles.body: By Jedidah JoshemCHENNAI: Once touted as the future of American tennis, Robin Montgomery is now on a mission to make her mark on the senior circuit. The former junior American No. 1 took a step in that direction on Tuesday, as she stunned fourth seeded Panna Udvary 6-4, 1-6, 6-1 to advance to the round of 16 at the WTA Chennai Open.At 22, Montgomery has already had her share of highs and lows. She won the junior US Open singles and doubles titles in 2021 as a 16-year-old which brought her to the cusp of stardom. But last year was about fighting back from a career-threatening wrist injury which forced her out of action for nearly 10 months. Reflecting on her journey, Montgomery feels setbacks have given her something beyond tennis. “Injuries happen, I think unfortunately for me I’ve been kind of prone to them, the wrist one being my biggest. But I took that time to learn new things about myself on and off the court,” she said after her win on Tuesday.“I haven’t played a full season. I’ve always been out for at least three months each year since I turned pro. Unfortunately, I did feel like I’m falling behind but I’m learning what’s right for me,” Montgomery, who won her first WTA 250 title in June this year at Libéma Open.She also highlighted how financial considerations, coaching arrangements and sponsorship support remain important aspects which need to be addressed in women’s tennis. Accompanied by just her boyfriend who also plays tennis, she pointed out that her coach Denis Kudla is currently not with her on tour.“When you have sponsorships, it means a lot, but with equal prize money right now, we’re definitely moving in the right direction but there’s always room for improvement.”Her introduction to tennis was nothing but a happenstance, when her mother, a single parent enrolled her in the sport, looking for a way to channel the energy of a hyperactive five-year-old. articles.title: Jodie Burrage: British tennis player receives death threats and social media abuse after defeat
articles.summary: Britain's Jodie Burrage receives death threats and abuse on social media after she is beaten in her first WTA Tour singles match proper for 16 months.
articles.body:
Britain's Jodie Burrage received death threats and abuse on social media after she was beaten in her first WTA Tour singles match proper for 16 months.

The 27-year-old, ranked 474th in the world, suffered a first-round exit at the Chennai Open after India's Vaishnavi Adkar fought back from a set down to triumph 3-6 6-3 7-5.

Burrage later shared a story on her Instagram account , external with a video scroll of direct messages, including abuse, she was sent following the match.

"Nice welcome back to tour. I remember why I left," said the Londoner in the accompanying message.

Germany's Eva Lys showed solidarity with Burrage, tagging the WTA from her Instagram handle and asking: "When will something be done?"

British number 15 Burrage's last match on the WTA Tour, excluding qualifiers, was in July 2025 when she lost to Catherine McNally in the first round at Wimbledon.

Female tennis players were subjected to more than 12,000 abusive posts and messages on social media last year, according to a report published earlier this year .

Data from the Signify Group's threat matrix service, which uses artificial intelligence-led detection, showed a similar number of abusive posts in 2025 to 2024.

A report from the same group two years ago found that angry gamblers were behind 48% of posts which were deemed to be abusive.

They were responsible for 42% of verified abuse in 2025 and 59% of cases of serious abuse.

In 2025, Britain's Katie Boulter told BBC Sport she had received death threats.

Fellow players called for identity verification to be introduced by social media platforms to try to address the issue.

The WTA's player board has previously condemned the abuse as "unacceptable" and said the impact can be "significant".

articles.title: Jodie Burrage: British player receives death threats and abuse on social media after Chennai Open first-round defeat
articles.summary: Jodie Burrage has revealed online abuse and death threats; both Burrage and fellow British player Katie Boulter believe most abuse comes from tennis gamblers who have lost money; Warning: This article contains details some readers may find distressing
articles.body:
Burrage, who was playing her first WTA Tour singles match in 16 months, went down against India's Vaishnavi Adkar.

She looked poised for victory when she led 5-3 in the deciding set but lost four games in a row to fall to a 3-6 6-3 7-5 defeat after two hours and 47 minutes.

The 27-year-old, who reached a career-high ranking 85 in September 2023, published an Instagram story with some of the abuse received due to the defeat.

"Nice welcome back to tour. I remember why I left," Burrage said in the accompanying message.

German player Eva Lys tagged the WTA from her Instagram handle and asked: "When will something be done?"

The 27-year-old appeared to struggle with the humid conditions and called the doctor with her opponent about to serve for the match.

Burrage was visibly shaking and had her blood pressure and oxygen levels checked as well as ice rubbed on her arms and legs. She was able to resume the contest but lost the final game to love.

Last July, Burrage urged gambling companies and social media companies to do more to tackle online trolls.

Speaking after her first-round defeat to American Caty McNally at Wimbledon, Burrage said she has had to stop herself from looking at her phone due to online abuse.

"I think it's very simple to have someone's ID connected to their account and that would, I think, quickly stop what people write and make them more accountable," Burrage said.

"I'm just guessing that they're gamblers; some of them say, 'You've lost me this amount of money' or whatever, so some of them are. I don't know, that's the only explanation I've got otherwise they are just very bad people.

"But yes, it's tough and today I'm trying not to look at my phone. It's not easy to deal with, but I do think there could be more being done."

A report from the Women's Tennis Association and International Tennis Federation revealed that 458 players were direct targets of abuse in 2024. The report, produced using an AI-led detection system developed by the Signify Group, found that 40 per cent of the social media abuse came from frustrated gamblers, a figure that rose to 77 per cent for direct abuse directed towards players' personal accounts.

Boulter believes much of the abuse comes from gamblers who have lost money and while she has learned how to better handle it over the years, incidents can raise genuine concerns for her safety.

"I think it just kind of shows how vulnerable we are. You really don't know if this person is on site. You really don't know if they're nearby or if they know where you live or anything like that," she said.

"At the very start of my career, it's probably something I took very personally [...] getting comments about the way you look."

"It becomes more apparent every single time you go on your phone."

The WTA's player board has previously condemned the abuse as "unacceptable" and said the impact can be "significant".

articles.title: WTA Finals in Indian Wells: Format, schedule, players, as Elena Rybakina and Aryna Sabalenka lead field at end-of-season event
articles.summary: The season-ending championship heads to Indian Wells for the first time, with new world No 1 Elena Rybakina leading the field along with Aryna Sabalenka and Coco Gauff; You can watch the WTA Finals live on Sky Sports from 8-15 November
articles.body:
The crown jewel of women's tennis takes place in Indian Wells, California with eight singles players and doubles teams having qualified in the Race to the Finals competing for tennis' ultimate prize.

Matches are played in a round-robin format between two groups of four, with the top two players or teams from each group moving on to the knockout stage.

Who will be crowned WTA Finals champion? Which singles star will raise the Billie Jean King Trophy?

Group 1 [1] Elena Rybakina [4] Coco Gauff [5] Jessica Pegula [8] Linda Noskova

Group 2 [2] Aryna Sabalenka [3] Mirra Andreeva [6] Elina Svitolina [7] Karolina Muchova

The 27-year-old arrives in the California desert as the world No 1 after bringing an end to Sabalenka's 99-week reign at the top. She captured both the Australian Open and the US Open - defeating rival Sabalenka in both finals.

2026 record: 49-14 Titles: 3 (Australian Open, Stuttgart, US Open) Previous WTA Finals appearances: 3 Best result: Champion (2025)

The Belarusian remains Rybakina's biggest threat after sweeping to victory at Indian Wells and Miami - becoming just the fifth woman in WTA history to complete the 'Sunshine Double'.

2026 record: 47-10 Titles: 3 (Brisbane, Indian Wells, Miami) Previous WTA Finals appearances: 5 Best result: Finalist (2022, 2025)

The American has all the momentum following a sensational second half of the year, highlighted by a title in Cincinnati and semi-final runs at both Wimbledon and the US Open.

2026 record: 47-15 Titles: 1 (Cincinnati) Previous WTA Finals appearances: 4 Best result: Champion (2024)

Three players will be making their tournament debuts with Andreeva leading the newcomers after securing her first Grand Slam title at the French Open.

2026 record: 50-16 Titles: 3 (Adelaide, Linz, Roland Garros) Previous WTA Finals appearances: 0

Her victory at the WTA 1000 event in Doha in February was just the second title of her career and her first since 2019. She then won a grass-court title in Bad Homburg before reaching her second Grand Slam final at Wimbledon in the summer.

2026 record: 40-11 Titles: 2 (Doha, Bad Homburg) Previous WTA Finals appearances: 0

The reigning Wimbledon champion also reached the semi-finals at Indian Wells earlier in the year and advanced to the US Open quarter-finals in September.

2026 record: 35-15 Titles: 2 (Berlin, Wimbledon) Previous WTA Finals appearances: 0

American Pegula reached 50 victories as well as making five finals, including titles in Dubai and Charleston before finishing runner-up in Berlin, Washington DC and Cincinnati. She also reached the US Open semi-finals for a second consecutive year and made the quarter-finals at Wimbledon and Rome.

2026 record: 50-13 Titles: 2 (Dubai, Charleston) Previous WTA Finals appearances: 4 Best result: Finalist (2023)

Svitolina is heading back to the season-ending event seven years after her last appearance. She went undefeated to win the title in 2018 and reached the final again a year later.

2026 record: 46-14 Titles: 2 (Auckland, Rome) Previous WTA Finals appearances: 3 Best result: Champion (2018)

Former Australian Open champion Madison Keys will join Sky Sports' broadcasting team with the 31-year-old offering viewers an insider's perspective as a commentator and analyst alongside Martina Navratilova, Marion Bartoli, commentator Jonathan Overend and Laura Robson.

Keys, who lifted the Daphne Akhurst Memorial Cup in 2025, remains an active competitor on the WTA Tour.

She won the Eastbourne title in June 2026 and reached the third round of the US Open in September. She is currently ranked No 24 in the world.

articles.title: "She was the hardest to win": Andre Agassi revealed why Steffi Graf saying yes meant more than winning a Grand Slam
articles.summary: Two years ago, Andre Agassi offered a glimpse into one of tennis's most enduring love stories, revealing that his greatest personal victory had nothing to
articles.body: Two years ago, Andre Agassi offered a glimpse into one of tennis's most enduring love stories, revealing that his greatest personal victory had nothing to do with lifting a Grand Slam trophy. For the eight-time major champion, winning Steffi Graf's heart was a challenge unlike anything he had faced on court. Their romance took years to develop, survived complicated personal circumstances and eventually grew into a marriage built on respect, humour and family. Even after decades together, Agassi's words made it clear that Graf remained his most meaningful achievement.Andre Agassi's pursuit of Steffi Graf began at Wimbledon in 1992The story began in 1992, when both tennis stars were enjoying remarkable success. Agassi had developed a strong attraction to Graf after watching her during a French television interview. He even tried to contact her following the 1991 French Open, but received no response.Their paths finally crossed after Agassi won his first Wimbledon men's singles title by defeating Goran Ivanišević. Graf had already claimed the women's championship. Agassi was excited about meeting her at the traditional Wimbledon Champions' Ball, where the winners usually shared a dance.However, the organisers cancelled the dance that year. Graf later joked about her role in the decision, saying, "I worked them real hard to cancel it," before explaining that she had never learned to dance properly.Although the two champions met and posed for photographs, romance did not follow immediately. Graf was dating racing driver Michael Bartels, while Agassi later married actress Brooke Shields in 1997. Their marriage ended in 1999.Steffi Graf became Andre Agassi's hardest-fought victoryTheir relationship took a new direction in 1999 when Agassi arranged a practice session with Graf during the Key Biscayne tournament in Florida. He began making efforts to get closer to her, sending flowers and carefully planning how to express his feelings.During a flight to London between the French Open and Wimbledon, Agassi even turned an airline menu into a birthday card for Graf. He eventually made his intentions clear, telling her:"So I need to tell you, I just need to say before we go any further, that I think you are beautiful. I respect you, I admire you, and I would absolutely love to get to know you better. That's my goal. That's my only agenda."Their romance developed quickly. Graf ended her relationship with Bartels, and the couple went public in September 1999.They married on October 22, 2001, in a private ceremony at Agassi's Las Vegas home, with their mothers serving as the only witnesses. Reflecting on the moment, Agassi told Forbes India, "She was the hardest to win… when Steffi Graf says yes, it's as close to arriving."The couple welcomed son Jaden four days after their wedding and daughter Jaz in 2003. They later focused on family life, charitable work and business ventures.Agassi summed up his admiration for Graf beautifully during her 2004 Women's Tennis Hall of Fame induction, saying, "You've spent many years of your life competing, but right here where we stand, in the ears of your children and right now in my heart, you have no rival."Graf returned the affection with her own memorable words: "Tennis has been a journey, and the best part of this journey is it led to you. I'll be forever grateful for that."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Pepo Clavet: "La pista de tenis es como un tablero de ajedrez"
articles.standfirst: El preparador madrileño ha ganado tres títulos en la banda de Davidovich esta temporada
articles.summary: El preparador madrileño ha ganado tres títulos en la banda de Davidovich esta temporada
articles.body: Pepo Clavet, de 61 años, empezó a tutelar la carrera de Alejandro Davidovich en la gira europea de hierba. Ganaron en Mallorca. Posteriormente llegaron dos títulos más en el ATP de Chengdu y Shanghái. El experimentado preparador madrileño habla con MARCA sobre el éxito logrado junto a su nuevo pupilo. Pregunta. Magnus Norman confiesa que desde pequeño tenía esa vocación de entrenador. ¿A usted le pasaba un poco igual? Respuesta. Me llegó después. En mi época de jugador no tenía ninguna vocación de entrenador. A mí lo que me encantaba era el tenis. Yo estaba entre el 200-300 y no se ganaba nada de dinero. Y con 25 años se me dio la oportunidad de trabajar con mi hermano Pato. Al principio me costaba porque a mí lo que realmente me gustaba era jugar. Poco a poco me fui acostumbrando y le encontré el gustillo al tema de entrenar y me encanta. P. ¿Cuánto tiempo lleva como técnico? R. Empecé con mi hermano a finales de 1991. Ya son 35 años. P. ¿Recuerda a todos los tenistas que ha ayudado? R. Más o menos. Pato, Corretja, Bruguera, Jacobo Díaz, Quino Muñoz, Guillermo García, Feliciano López, Fernando Verdasco, Carlos Costa, Tommy Robredo, Karen Khachanov, Pico Mónaco... Y en chicas con Vivi, mi mujer, y Gala León. Las otras chicas con las que estuve fueron Anna Chakvetadze y Olga Danilovic. P. ¿Tiene contados los títulos que ha ganado desde la banda? R. No lo sé, la verdad. Nunca me he sentado un día con un papel y un lápiz a contarlos. Lo que sí sé es que gané con mi hermano Pato, con Verdasco, con Corretja, con Robredo, con Feli, con Khachanov y ahora con Álex. P. Usted que tiene una vida tan sacrificada, con tantos viajes, ¿le ayuda que su mujer haya sido tenista profesional? R. Me ayuda mucho porque ella entiende cómo es este mundo y que pueda estar fuera cinco semanas seguidas. La suerte del tenis actual es que la mayoría de los equipos están formado por dos entrenadores. Eso me permite estar libre algunas semanas, como la actual, en la que es Pato quien estaba en París con Davidovich. P. Cuando tuvo que proponer un segundo entrenador para Álex, ¿tuvo claro que el mejor era su hermano? R. Yo lo que siempre he intentado en los equipos es crear un buen ambiente. Los entrenadores tienen que estar en la misma página y transmitir el mismo mensaje al jugador. De otra manera, el tenista se lía. Es muy importante, aunque no fácil, que el jugador vea que hay muy buena sintonía en todo el equipo. P. En el ranking de los más talentosos que ha entrenado, ¿Davidovich está el primero? R. Álex me ha sorprendido porque, comparándolo a un restaurante, el menú de su carta es muy amplio. Tiene muchos golpes, tiene muchas jugadas, tiene un físico muy bueno, aunque hay que cuidarlo. No sé si es el más talentoso que he entrenado, pero seguro que de los que más. P. ¿Han trabajado más el aspecto mental que tenístico? R. Sí, sobre todo teniendo en cuenta de que yo empecé en mitad de la temporada. No puedes tener muchos días de entrenamiento para trabajar ciertos aspectos que pueden ser mejorables a nivel técnico y táctico. He intentado transmitirle mensajes de confianza. Yo siempre le digo: ‘llevo 36 años entrenando y a mí no me van a decir lo que tú puedes jugar. Yo sé, por mi experiencia, el tenis que puedes desarrollar. Otra cosa es que tú quieras hacerlo’. El espíritu de lucha que demostró en los últimos torneos, y en especial en Shanghái, donde iba set abajo con Hurkacz, luego con Zverev y después con Jódar, quizá en otro momento de su carrera se hubiese dejado llevar. Luchó y luchó y se llevó el título. P. ¿En qué ayuda el ajedrez en el tenis? R. A mí el ajedrez siempre me ha gustado. Álex también es aficionado. Yo creo que ayuda en la paciencia, en el saber estar, analizando la situación global. La pista es cómo el tablero y a ver cómo te juega el contrario. El tenis es un deporte táctico dentro de la velocidad a la que se juega actualmente. P. ¿Usted y Davidovich tienen un nivel parejo? R. Digamos que le gano. Las partidas dramáticas eran con Toni Nadal, eso sí que eran partidas de ajedrez. P. ¿Qué techo tenístico le ve a su jugador, puede ganar un Grand Slam? R. Por qué no. Es evidente que es muy difícil, pero a la vez está más abierto que en la época de Federer, Djokovic y Nadal. Están Sinner y Alcaraz, pero este año se ha llevado dos Zverev. El objetivo es estar en el top10', poder jugar el Masters de Turín. Son objetivos que a mí me encantan. Es verdad que meten presión, pero es relativa. Es mucho mejor este tipo de presión que no por salir fuera del 100 o estar el 200 y no saber si te compensa seguir jugando a tenis. Es una presión que si la sabes llevar es muy bonita. P. ¿Cómo entrenador le haría ilusión que Álex ganara la Copa Davis? R. Mucho. La Copa Davis es un torneo que se juega por equipos, que representas a tu país, que formas equipo con grandes jugadores... Me hace una ilusión increíble que esté dentro del equipo. Son uno de los máximos favoritos para ganar la Davis.
